intro.heading: The inspector's question is simple. The answer is not.
intro.sub: A scenario we see in many care settings.
intro.paragraph: Asha manages a care home. Training certificates sit in each staff folder, and she keeps a spreadsheet with a coloured square for every person and every course. It looked fine in March. Then three carers joined, a fire safety certificate ran out and nobody changed a colour. A visit could come any week. Asha does not need a prettier grid. She needs a staff training matrix that is true today, and a way to hand it over without a scramble.

trail.text: Everyone completes the mandatory courses and certificates go into staff folders.
Asha builds a spreadsheet with a coloured square for each person and course.
The squares are green and the team feels well prepared.
Three new carers join. Nobody adds their rows to the sheet.
A fire safety certificate expires. The square stays green.
Colours change by hand, when someone remembers to open the file.
Nobody can say who is due for renewal in the next two months.
"Can I see who is in date for safeguarding and moving and handling?"

trail_close: The training happened. The record of it drifted. A grid that is edited by hand cannot tell you what is true today. Here is how CareStream builds it from the records themselves, and where it stops.

why.heading: A matrix you maintain by hand is a matrix you cannot trust
why.sub: The question is not whether training took place. It is whether you can show it, today, without a scramble.

cards.title: Colours go stale the day after you edit
cards.body: A spreadsheet does not know a certificate has expired or that a new carer has started. Someone has to notice, and busy managers do not notice everything.

cards.title: The questions come fast and in pieces
cards.body: Who has not done safeguarding? Who is due next month? Which seniors are missing moving and handling? Answering from folders and a spreadsheet takes far longer than the question did.

cards.title: Good records help staffing, not only inspections
cards.body: A clear matrix shows who is safe to put on a shift and who needs a refresher booked. The staffing use of a matrix matters every week, not once a year.

talk.heading: The questions managers ask, and how CareStream answers them
talk.sub: Read this as a conversation. The questions are the ones we hear most.

items.q: I already have a spreadsheet. Why change?
items.a: Your spreadsheet only changes when someone edits it. The CareStream matrix reads completions recorded in the system, so a certificate that passes its date shows as Expired without anyone touching a colour.

items.q: Is this a training matrix template I can download?
items.a: Not as a blank file. A template is empty and you fill it in. Here you set the training each job role needs and the grid fills itself from what staff complete. You can still export the result to CSV and use your own spreadsheet.

items.q: What does each colour or symbol mean?
items.a: In date, Renewal due soon (within 60 days), Expired, Overdue, Practical to sign off, In progress, Assigned, not started, Required, not assigned, and Not required. A legend sits under the grid, and the same labels are printed on the PDF.

items.q: Does it include training my staff did somewhere else?
items.a: Only what is recorded in CareStream. That means courses staff complete in the Staff Hub and face to face sessions you log with who attended. A certificate sitting in a folder, or a course done elsewhere, does not appear unless it is recorded.

items.q: Will it enrol my staff on the training they are missing?
items.a: No. A red ! tells you a course is required but not assigned. You then allocate it. Setting requirements by role changes what the grid expects, it does not enrol anyone for you.

items.q: Can I hand it to an inspector?
items.a: You can download a CSV or print the grid to PDF, so you have something to show. It is a view of your own records. It is not a rating and it is not a regulator record.

items.q: What if a person has no job role set?
items.a: They only match the training you ticked for All staff. The role screen warns you how many staff have no job role, so you can set them on the Staff page.

items.q: Can I try it, and which plan has it?
items.a: Yes. There is a 14 day free trial, and you can create a free account to look around. Plans differ, so see the pricing page for which plan includes the matrix and required training by role.

limits.heading: A clear view of your records, not a substitute for the training

cards.title: It only knows what is recorded
cards.body: The matrix reflects courses completed in CareStream and face to face sessions you log. Training done elsewhere shows up only if it is recorded, so a gap on the grid may be a gap in the recording.

cards.title: It does not enrol anyone for you
cards.body: Required, not assigned tells you what to allocate. You still allocate it. A role requirement tells the grid what to expect, nothing more.

cards.title: It is not a rating or a regulator record
cards.body: A full green grid does not mean a pass, and the matrix is not a CQC document. It also cannot tell you whether the training changed what someone does on the floor.

items.q: What is a matrix of staff training in a care home?
items.a: A grid of staff against the training their job needs, showing what is complete, what is due and what has lapsed. CareStream builds it from your own training records in the system and your required training by role.

items.q: What should a staff training matrix show?
items.a: Each person, their job role, each required course and its status, with renewal dates where a course expires. See what a care home training matrix should contain for a fuller list.

items.q: Can I use a training matrix template instead?
items.a: You can, but a template is only as accurate as the last edit. If you want to compare approaches first, read whether an Excel matrix is still safe.

items.q: Where are the training records for one person?
items.a: On their staff record, under Required training for their role. It uses the same rules as the grid, so the two agree.

items.q: How do I set which courses each role needs?
items.a: In Training, open the Matrix tab and choose Required training by role. Pick a job role or All staff, tick the courses and save. The grid then shows only courses that some role requires.
Yes. Download a CSV, or use Print / PDF for a clean landscape page. Both follow your filters for name, job role and gaps only.

items.q: How does it treat face to face training?
items.a: Topics marked mandatory for a role on the Face-to-face tab appear in the grid, using attendance and renewal dates. Read more about recording in person sessions.
Please check the pricing page for which plan includes the matrix and required training by role, as plans change.

guide.heading: A practical way to get your matrix ready before an inspection
guide.lede: Start with what you are asked for, then work backwards to the records. These steps take an afternoon, and they make the grid worth trusting.

sections.h3: Start from the rules that apply to you
paragraphs: Regulation 18 of the Health and Social Care Act 2008 (Regulated Activities) Regulations 2014 says staff must receive such appropriate support, training, professional development, supervision and appraisal as is necessary to carry out their duties. Regulation 17 on good governance includes keeping securely the records that are necessary in relation to persons employed.

Those two lines are why a manager keeps training records at all. They do not give you a list of courses. Decide the list yourself, by job role, using your service and your policies. Then see the monthly compliance audit for a regular check.

sections.h3: Before the visit, work through this list
checklist: Check every staff member has a job role set, so the right requirements apply to them
Tick the courses each role needs, and All staff for training everyone holds
Assign anything marked Required, not assigned, then chase Expired and Overdue first
Export a CSV or print to PDF, and check a few rows against the certificates in staff folders

sections.h3: Keep it true after the visit
paragraphs: Open the grid on the same day each month and filter to gaps only. Book renewals for anyone in the 60 day window, and record in person sessions on the day they happen. Our guide to the Care Certificate course shows where new starters begin.

guide.note: CareStream gives you a view of your own records. It does not decide what training your service needs, and it does not promise any inspection outcome.
